questions.question_text: Determine whether $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 1, & x \le 2 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x > 2 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 2$.

options.text: Discontinuous at $x = 2$, because the subfunctions are defined by different algebraic formulas.
options.why: Assumed having different formulas automatically creates a discontinuity regardless of values.

options.text: Discontinuous at $x = 2$, because the left branch evaluates to $4$ and the right branch to $5$.
options.why: Made an arithmetic error evaluating $3(2) - 1$ as $4$ instead of $5$.

options.text: Discontinuous at $x = 2$, because $x > 2$ is a strict inequality.
options.why: Confused a strict domain inequality with a graph discontinuity.

questions.solution_text:
Evaluate both subfunctions at $x = 2$:
Left branch: $3(2) - 1 = 5$
Right branch: $(2)^{2} + 1 = 5$
Since both branches agree at $y = 5$, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 2$.

options.why: Stated the $y$-value of the filled dot instead of the $x$-value of the discontinuity.
Pointed to the $y$-intercept rather than the point of discontinuity.
Pointed to the left boundary of the plotted window instead of the discontinuity.

questions.solution_text:
Looking at the graph, there is a visible break and jump at $x = 1$.
$x = 1$

options.why: Confused a removable single-point hole with a jump where branch limits differ.
Mistook a bounded hole for an unbounded vertical asymptote.
Ignored the isolated point and open circle on the curve.

questions.solution_text:
At $x = 2$, the curve approaches $y = 2$ from both the left and right, but $g(2) = 4$.
This represents a removable discontinuity (hole).

questions.question_text: Find the value of $k$ that makes $f(x) = \begin{cases} kx + 1, & x \le 2 \\ x^{2} - 3, & x > 2 \end{cases}$ continuous at $x = 2$.

options.why: Solved $2k + 1 = 1$ incorrectly as $2k = 2 \implies k = 1$.
Made a sign error when solving $2k = 0$.
Evaluated the right branch as $2^{2} + 3 = 7$ instead of $2^{2} - 3 = 1$, giving $2k + 1 = 7$ and $k = 3$.

questions.solution_text:
Set the two subfunctions equal at $x = 2$:
$k(2) + 1 = (2)^{2} - 3$
$2k + 1 = 4 - 3$
$2k + 1 = 1$
$2k = 0$
$k = 0$

questions.question_text: At which values of $x$ is the rational function $f(x) = \dfrac{5}{x^{2} - 5x}$ discontinuous?

options.why: Divided by $x$ and forgot that $x = 0$ makes the denominator zero.
Found $x = 0$ but omitted the second root $x = 5$ of $x(x - 5) = 0$.
Confused $x^{2} - 5x$ with the difference of squares $x^{2} - 25$.

questions.solution_text:
Set the denominator equal to zero:
$x^{2} - 5x = 0$
$x(x - 5) = 0$
$x = 0$ or $x = 5$

questions.question_text: Determine all values of $x$ where $f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 9}{x^{2} - 4}$ is discontinuous.

options.why: Set the numerator equal to zero instead of the denominator.
Omitted the negative root when solving $x^{2} = 4$.
Combined the zeroes of both the numerator and the denominator.

questions.solution_text:
Discontinuities occur where the denominator is zero:
$x^{2} - 4 = 0$
$(x - 2)(x + 2) = 0$
$x = -2, 2$

questions.question_text: Classify the discontinuity in $f(x) = \begin{cases} 4 - x, & x < 1 \\ x^{2} + 4, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$ at $x = 1$.

options.why: Assumed the discontinuity can be fixed with a single point, but the left and right values differ.
Mistook a finite step change for an infinite vertical asymptote.
Evaluated $4 - 1 = 3$ and $1^{2} + 4 = 5$ but incorrectly concluded they are equal.

questions.solution_text:
Evaluate left and right branches at $x = 1$:
Left branch: $4 - 1 = 3$
Right branch: $1^{2} + 4 = 5$
Since $3 \neq 5$, there is a jump discontinuity at $x = 1$.

questions.question_text: Find the values of $a$ and $b$ so that $f(x) = \begin{cases} ax - 1, & x \le 2 \\ 5, & 2 < x \le 4 \\ x^{2} - b, & x > 4 \end{cases}$ is continuous everywhere.

options.why: Dropped the $-1$ when matching at $x = 2$, solving $2a = 4$ instead of $2a - 1 = 5$, giving $a = 2$.
Sign error at $x = 4$: rearranged $5 = 16 - b$ as $b = 5 - 16 = -11$ instead of $b = 16 - 5$.
Made both slips at once: dropped the $-1$ at $x = 2$ and then rearranged $5 = 16 - b$ the wrong way at $x = 4$.

questions.solution_text:
For continuity at $x = 2$:
$2a - 1 = 5$
$2a = 6$
$a = 3$
For continuity at $x = 4$:
$5 = (4)^{2} - b$
$5 = 16 - b$
$b = 11$
$a = 3$ and $b = 11$

questions.question_text:
For what values of $a$ and $b$ is $f(x)$ continuous everywhere?
$f(x)=\begin{cases}2&x\le-1\\ax+b&-1<x<3\\-2&x\ge3\end{cases}$

options.why: Matches neither boundary value consistently with the linear section.
Reverses the required slope and gives the wrong value at both joins.
Makes the middle section constant at negative two instead of joining both endpoints.

questions.solution_text: Continuity at $x=-1$ requires $-a+b=2$. Continuity at $x=3$ requires $3a+b=-2$. Subtracting gives $4a=-4$, so $a=-1$; then $1+b=2$, giving $b=1$.

questions.question_text: Consider the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2&-1\le x<0\\2x&0\le x<1\\1&x=1\\-2x+4&1<x<2\\0&2<x<3.\end{cases}$ For what values of $x$ is $f(x)$ continuous?

options.text: All real values of x, except for $x=1$
options.why: Also omits x=2, where the piecewise function is not defined.

options.text: All real values of x, except for $x=0,1$ and 2
options.why: At x=0 the left and right limits both equal the defined value 0.

options.text: All real values of x, except for $x=1$ and 2

options.why: At x=1 the limiting value is 2 but the defined value is 1, so continuity fails.

questions.solution_text: At $x=0$, the limits from both sides are 0 and $f(0)=0$, so the function is continuous. At $x=1$, both neighbouring formulas tend to 2 but $f(1)=1$, so it is discontinuous. At $x=2$, the function is not defined. Hence it is continuous at all real values in its domain except $x=1$ and $x=2$.
